subject: The hunger for power: however much you feed, the stomach never fills
alt: Satish Acharya's cartoon: on a grey background a big, white-bearded leader (in the manner of Narendra Modi, wearing glasses) sits on the floor with his mouth wide open, eating with a golden spoon. In front of him is a large golden bowl marked POWER in swirling letters, brimming with yellow dal and rice. From the right a hand tilts another golden bowl marked DELIMITATION, and dal and rice pour from it into the POWER bowl. At the lower left a small white-bearded man in an orange jacket stands pointing upwards; a speech bubble from him reads: YOUR HUNGER IS SUCH THAT NO MATTER HOW MUCH YOU FEED, THE STOMACH IS NEVER FULL! Near the leader's face is written BUURP. The cartoonist's signature, SATISH ACHARYA, is at the bottom left.
chutki: On a grey ground sits a big leader, mouth open, a golden spoon in hand, and in front of him the bowl marked POWER, which never fills. From the right the bowl marked DELIMITATION is tilted over, and the leader's stomach says only: BUURP. The small man standing below, finger raised, says: however much you feed him, the stomach is never full.

This is the picture of the hunger for power, with delimitation - the redrawing of seats - as its excuse. Satish Acharya has named the very bowls POWER and DELIMITATION, and put the whole debate in one place: for those who hold delimitation in their hands, it is not a means but a meal.
